faq.q: Which products work well with relighting?
faq.a: Glass, metal, ceramic and glossy items can show useful changes in highlight and shadow.

faq.q: Do I need a studio setup?
faq.a: No. A clear phone photo can become a softly lit product image without a studio setup.

faq.q: Can I fix glare on glass or metal?
faq.a: The generated image can soften highlights and keep the product face easier to read, but reflective results still need review.

faq.q: Do I need real studio lights?
faq.a: No. The lighting is generated from the uploaded photo and the job uses credits instead of a lighting kit.

faq.q: What does a relit photo cost?
faq.a: Each product relighting photo costs 24 credits, shown before you run the job.

faq.q: Will relighting change my product shape or color?
faq.a: Generated highlights can shift a reflective surface. Compare the result with the real item when shape, color or finish must be exact.

faq.q: Which lighting scene suits an Amazon listing?
faq.a: Even front fill with a readable product face suits a listing image; reserve dramatic highlights for ads and detail pages.

faq.q: Can relighting fix glare on glass or metal?
faq.a: It can reshape highlights while keeping the uploaded product as the subject. Review the label and edges at full size.

steps.prompt: Place the uploaded bottle beside a bright window with a soft highlight on its glass.
